summary: John Morrison worked in Indology and religious studies, earning a D.D. at the University of Calcutta. He served as Principal of Scottish Church College (1889–1904) and held lectureships at the University of Glasgow (1904) and the University of Edinburgh.

John Muir studied at East India Company College, Fort William College, Glasgow, and Bonn. He served in the Bengal Civil Service (1828–1853), was Principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1844), and founded the University of Edinburgh in 1862.

Active in Indology and religious studies, John Murdoch was educated at the High School of Glasgow and the University of Glasgow (LL.D. 1878). He served as Agent and Travelling Secretary for the Christian Vernacular Education Society (1858–1903) and was a Fellow of the University of Madras.

John Murray Mitchell worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Aberdeen Grammar School, Marischal College, the University of Aberdeen, and the University of Edinburgh. He taught at Wilson College, Mumbai (1844–1866) and served as Principal of Duff College (1868–1873).

Working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, John Myrdhin Reynolds studied under traditional teachers Yongdzin Tenzin Namdak, Dudjom Rinpoche, and Namkhai Norbu. He also founded the Bonpo Translation Project.

John N. Carpenter worked in religious studies and Indology. A missionary with the Church Mission Society, he held posts at St. John's College, Agra, and served as Principal of St. Paul's Divinity School (1900) and Emmanuel College (1916–1922).

Nemec works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned degrees from Rochester (BA), UC Santa Barbara (MA), Oxford (MPhil), and Pennsylvania (PhD 2005), studying under Alexis Sanderson and Ludo Rocher. In 2004, he became Associate Professor at the University of Virginia.

Linguist John Okell studied at The Queen's College, Oxford, and under Hla Pe, Anna J. Allott, and Richard Keith Sprigg. He served as a research associate at SOAS University of London from 1959 to 1999.

Working in Buddhist and religious studies, John P. Keenan earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota. He was a research fellow at Nanzan University (1983–1986) and later taught religious studies at Middlebury College.

Peile worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Christ's College, Cambridge, and under Theodor Benfey at Göttingen. At Cambridge, he became Reader of Comparative Philology (1884–1893) and Master of Christ's College (1887), later serving as President of Newnham College.
John Penry Lewis was a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He earned a B.A. from Queen's University Belfast (~1872–1876) and served in the Ceylon Civil Service from 1877 to 1910.

John Peter Jones was an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Case Western Reserve University and Andover Theological Seminary. He served as Principal of Pasumalai Seminary (1892–1914) and became Professor of Indian Missions at Hartford Seminary in 1914.

John Peter Wade worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied medicine at the University of Edinburgh and served as an Assistant Medical Surgeon for the East India Company beginning in 1784.

Indologist John Pickford studied at Oxford and Brasenose College under Monier Monier-Williams. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Presidency College, Chennai, until 1872, and was also a professor at the University of Madras.

John Playfair studied at the University of St Andrews, St Mary's College, and the University of Edinburgh. He co-founded the Royal Society of Edinburgh in 1783 and served as Professor of Mathematics at the University of Edinburgh from 1785 to 1818.

Powers studied at Holy Cross, McMaster, and Virginia (PhD under Jeffrey Hopkins). Working in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, he held posts at ANU (1995–2016), Deakin University (2016–2022), and Melbourne (2022).

A scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, John R. B. Campbell earned his PhD at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and Gary A. Tubb. He also trained under the 14th Dalai Lama, among other traditional teachers.

John R. McRae specialized in Buddhist studies and sinology, completing his Ph.D. at Yale under Stanley Weinstein. He taught at Cornell, Indiana University Bloomington, and Komazawa University, and chaired the Numata Center and Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai.
John Riley Perks is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Working in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, John Ronald Newman earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundup Sopa. He held posts at UW-Madison (attested 1987) and New College of Florida (attested 1996–2000).
